questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Having the opportunity to take part in an internship with practical fieldwork and hands-on experience with great resources and facilities in a great and interesting location was the main reason in choosing Svalbard. Additionally, I wanted to get to know the location in which I will be staying for 5 months next year as part of my masters thesis work.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The overall study abroad experience was great! Really enjoyed Svalbard, it has great resources at the university and the accommodation, and they are always helpful when you need something. The location is very remote and the only reason the experience isn't a 9 or 10 is that the recreational side of Svalbard is limited with requiring a rifle and flare gun to go outside the town for hikes as well as no real social or recreational groups available.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was either provided prior to my arrival by my supervisor during calls, from the university through informative emails or from the accommodation through emails as well. Additionally, it is easy to acquire information from other students in addition to the reception at UNIS who are always happy to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received little assistance apart from a short tour of the town from my supervisor on the 2nd day. Most relevant information was provided to me beforehand. I got the airport bus into town on the first day which cost 70 NOK for students and was very easy to use.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: My orientation was sufficient however that was due to my supervisor taking care of me and explaining everything in this aspect. For students that are going to study there, I believe it is a bit more difficult and you need to seek information from reception at UNIS.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Housing is provided and guaranteed for all UNIS students at Elvesletta student accommodation which is in the centre of town and about 300 metres from the UNIS building.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a shared kitchen area in the accommodation in which you can cook your own meals. No meal plans are provided apart from a small area at UNIS where you can just get lunches when you are on campus. The basics are in the kitchens e.g. microwave, stove, oven, fridges, freezers sink etc. also the oil, salt and spices are left from previous people alongside random food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The accommodation is very modern, and I stayed in a single room with my own bathroom while sharing a kitchen with 7 other people. They installed a new study area in the accommodation, which was great and the facilities such as laundry, drying areas were great as well. The accommodation is one of the best aspects of being a student in Svalbard.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did not take any courses and therefore I do not know of that process however, registering for the internship was relatively easy through my supervisor. I had to fill in an application form describing what I will do during my stay, what my goals are and a reviewing procedure.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was help from my supervisor as well as UNIS reception is very helpful alongside student administrators who you can find in their offices most days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not take classes and therefore do not know about this process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and have a contact person from UNIS help you through it as it can be a little bit confusing. Email UNIS reception or study administrators who are very attentive and quick to reply.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Did not take a course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Do not know the style of teaching as I did not take a course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I know for students staying in the Spring semester, it is highly recommended to take the Arctic safety course in the middle of January where you have an intensive week of safety training where you learn how to shoot a rifle, drive a snowmobile, how to survive if you fall in the ice etc.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you come prepared with all the necessary gear, no costs are unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Not more than I expected but food and especially fresh fruit and vegetables are really expensive due to the isolated nature of the town. I would recommend buying the frozen vegetables for this as they are much cheaper. However due to the lack of paying taxes, the outdoor gear as well as alcohol is relatively cheap compared to mainland Norway.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: While there is a gym in the town, there are no cultural, athletic and social activity groups for students available. You have to really make your own group with people, the most popular activity in the summer is hiking while in the spring I know skiing and snow mobile trips are very popular. There is a big Facebook messenger group chat with all the students in Svalbard in which you can try and meet people outside your classes. Additionally, most people party on Friday nights, so that is also a good place to meet people to make a group of friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely find a group and go hiking around Longyearbyen and beyond if you are there in the summer as it is amazing views and a great way to explore the island.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, go on a ferry around the island and go in the sauna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as you are constantly around internationals in the accommodation and the culture is very much like Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are no real local students, they are all internationals. Just go out and meet people, you will find everyone in the same accommodation so its easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, it is the same as an international student at KU

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is an international student and in the same boat. Everyone is very open.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be ready for cold weather and make sure to bring appropriate clothes although you can buy outdoor and warm clothes there. Food is very expensive, be aware of this. The expenses can stack up without you even noticing. Lastly, you NEED a rifle to go out of town and it is highly recommended and required in some instances that you need another person to go with you. Don't go past the polar bear warning signs without being prepared.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to contact UNIS reception and the student services as they are really helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The beautiful landscapes and amazing wildlife.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The weather.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
